standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic cleaning-product safety task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner and a trusted adult gather two or more real cleaning products from the household, read each label together for its active ingredient and warning text, sort the products into pairs that are safe to use in the same space and pairs that must never be combined, and then, under the adult's direct supervision, use one product on a real surface exactly as its label directs, including ventilation and any dwell time.
safetyNotes: Never mix a bleach-based product with an ammonia-based product, such as many glass or window cleaners; combining them produces dangerous fumes.
Use any cleaning product only in a space with a window open or a fan running, never in a closed room with no airflow.
If any accidental mixing happens, or you notice a strong or unusual smell, stop immediately, leave the area, and get a trusted adult right away.

simulationAlternative.description: If the household has only one cleaning product on hand, the learner instead reads that product's label in detail with a trusted adult, identifies every hazard symbol and warning present, and writes which categories of other common products, naming the category rather than combining anything, would be unsafe to mix with it and why.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific hazard warning from a label in this task that you had not paid attention to before, and how it would change what you do next time you clean.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Hazard identification and never-mix reasoning: At least one real never-mix pair is correctly identified with a reason drawn from the actual label text. | Safe, supervised product use: The product is used exactly as the label directs, with a trusted adult supervising the entire time. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner and trusted adult review one more product not used in this task, add its hazard category to the never-mix list, and explain where in the household that product should be stored so it stays separated from anything it should never contact.

resources.title: cleaning-product safety worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner and a trusted adult gather two or more real cleaning products from the household, read each label together for its active ingredient and warning text, sort the products into pairs that are safe to use in the same space and pairs that must never be combined, and then, under the adult's direct supervision, use one product on a real surface exactly as its label directs, including ventilation and any dwell time.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact cleaning-product safety decision or action.
Model move 2: With your trusted adult, gather two or more real cleaning products from the household and read one label fully together.
Model move 3: With your trusted adult, sort the gathered products into pairs that are safe to have in the same space and pairs that must never be combined, based on what each label says.

Model check: Hazard identification and never-mix reasoning: At least one real never-mix pair is correctly identified with a reason drawn from the actual label text. | Safe, supervised product use: The product is used exactly as the label directs, with a trusted adult supervising the entire time.

resources.title: cleaning-product safety action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for cleaning-product safety.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: cleaning-product safety coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner and a trusted adult gather two or more real cleaning products from the household, read each label together for its active ingredient and warning text, sort the products into pairs that are safe to use in the same space and pairs that must never be combined, and then, under the adult's direct supervision, use one product on a real surface exactly as its label directs, including ventilation and any dwell time.
Coach direction: With your trusted adult, gather two or more real cleaning products from the household and read one label fully together.
Learner prompt: Name the product you read closely, its active ingredient if listed, and one specific warning printed on its label.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: cleaning-product safety complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your trusted adult, sort the gathered products into pairs that are safe to have in the same space and pairs that must never be combined, based on what each label says.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I identified at least one pair of products, or product categories, that must never be mixed, and named why, based on their labels.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My trusted adult reviewed my sorting before I used any product.

Equal-access rule: If the household has only one cleaning product on hand, the learner instead reads that product's label in detail with a trusted adult, identifies every hazard symbol and warning present, and writes which categories of other common products, naming the category rather than combining anything, would be unsafe to mix with it and why.

resources.title: cleaning-product safety minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific hazard warning from a label in this task that you had not paid attention to before, and how it would change what you do next time you clean.

Success checks: Hazard identification and never-mix reasoning: At least one real never-mix pair is correctly identified with a reason drawn from the actual label text. | Safe, supervised product use: The product is used exactly as the label directs, with a trusted adult supervising the entire time.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: cleaning-product safety supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional cleaning-product safety condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Hazard identification and never-mix reasoning: At least one real never-mix pair is correctly identified with a reason drawn from the actual label text. | Safe, supervised product use: The product is used exactly as the label directs, with a trusted adult supervising the entire time..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u02-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
